title: In peace, roads are never dangerous, so patrols have nothing to reduce
what: Route danger starts only above 0.55 after security relief (at most 0.25). A war-front siege (0.85) always clears it; an occupation only while contested or unstable; war exhaustion only with high crime or the trade-hub premium; crime plus premium never. The tuning comment says siege or occupation alone always clears it, which the occupation weight contradicts. All drivers are war-layer ledgers, so in a realm that has never held a live war front (RR without War) dispatch refusal, banditry, interception and smuggling spill do not fire. Host: src/domain/spatial/embattlement.js:84-98, :84-86, :113-115, :196-206, :237-245; src/domain/worldPulse/pulseKernel.js:2366-2389.

title: One territory or two?
what: Host gates come from an unbudgeted nearest-by-cost partition with no wild land; the map's W8 territory has unclaimed land and contested marches. If W8 were fed to the host as its territory, towns across unclaimed land would lose their gate and the caravan graph could break. Proposal: supply a routing partition for the host and the political territory as a lens and as rule facts; otherwise the host must treat wild cells as passable non-gates (a host change).

when: Owner and host to decide.

title: Would the host adopt patrol coverage?
what: Caravan routing has no patrol term. The only nearby slot is the embattlement ramp's security relief (0.4 x security, capped at 0.25), fed from one minus defense pressure, and it matters only where war drives danger. Designed but unfed slots: TR-1's route_wardenship / route_predation pairs (registered, no producer) and EC-6's route_wardenship stance term (unowned, OD-FC-2). The note proposes offering J378's patrol coverage per route segment as a producer for those slots or as a security input, keyed to the host's gates, not to map road lines.
why: Without adoption, patrols drawn on the map change nothing in the simulation.
when: Host to decide whether to adopt, and in which slot.
